name: GameStop Corp.
sector: Consumer Discretionary / Specialty retail — video games & collectibles
moat_justification: Narrow collectibles distribution and brand/community advantages, but no pricing power in its historic core: platform owners control digital game distribution, ROIC was negative for five straight years before a first positive +5.55% in FY2026, and revenue is structurally shrinking — a financing/survival advantage from the cash pile is not an operating moat.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 21.7%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 1.04 vs 3-yr median 0.29 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
BIG_NET_CASH: net cash is 3.5x normalized OE — part of the price is a cash pile, not the operating business; note it in the verdict
one_liner: Improving but moatless retailer (moat 2/10) — even on the generous TTM base it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 6.34%, IV@15% $8.28 vs $26.81 price; clears 15% only below $8.28); the price is a cash/investment-asset and meme story, not owner's earnings.
moat_for: Largest specialty footprint for collectibles/trading cards with PSA grading partnership — collectibles 45.1% of Q2 (ended 2026-08-01) sales, +57% YoY
Recognized brand, loyal community and trade-in/pre-owned network rivals cannot easily replicate in physical retail
Fortress liquidity (cash $6.305B at FY2026 end) funds the pivot and removes distress risk
moat_against: Platform owners (Steam, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo) control digital distribution — no pricing power in hardware/software, the historic core
ROIC proxy negative 2021-2025 (-64.6%, -77.5%, -110.5%, -4.0%, -13.2%), only +5.55% in FY2026 — below cost of capital through the cycle
Revenue structurally shrinking: 5-yr CAGR -6.53%, 3-yr -15.04%, TTM -7.7% YoY; store fleet cut from ~3,203 to 2,206 in FY2026 alone
Collectibles concentration and fad risk — one category now carries the margin story
Supplier allocation dependence for cards and hardware; no owned product or platform
